turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same n-i-p (regular) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
The highest-efficiency MAPbI3 n-i-p cells in the training set share a small number of physically well-motivated features: a pinhole-free compact hole-blocking layer, an electron-selective contact whose conduction-band edge and surface chemistry minimise interface recombination (SnO2 nanoparticles, PCBM or C60), a hole-selective layer whose HOMO is well matched to the perovskite valence band and that can be doped or buffered for high conductivity (Spiro-MeOTAD, PTAA or the PCDTBT family), a chemically inert high-work-function back contact (Au or MoO3/Au), and a deposition sequence capable of producing compact, low-defect absorber films (spin-coating or co-evaporation). Flexible substrates, carbon electrodes, missing selective contacts and chemically reactive ZnO without a protective interlayer are consistently associated with far lower medians.

These criteria immediately isolate five pool entries whose stacks are near-duplicates of the training champions (20.85 %, 19.35 %, 18.19 %, 17.9 %):

- c064 reproduces the unique TiO2-c | SnO2-np bilayer that gave the record 20.85 % cell (SnO2 contacts the perovskite, compact TiO2 guarantees shunt-free coverage) together with Spiro-MeOTAD and Au.
- c005 is identical to the 19.35 % device except for the minor ITO/FTO and PCDTBT8/PCDTBT1 substitutions; the TiO2/PCBM cascade plus MoO3/Au contact remains intact.
- c068 combines the two highest-performing selective contacts in the data (SnO2 and PTAA) on glass with an Au-based electrode.
- c017 is a near-copy of the 17.9 % co-evaporated C60 / doped-TaTm cell (only Ag versus Au).
- c080 places a compact TiO2 / C60-type fullerene contact under Spiro-MeOTAD/Ag, matching the 17.2 % analogue.

No other candidate simultaneously satisfies band alignment, interface passivation, contact chemistry and film-quality constraints at this level.

Final: c064, c005, c068, c017, c080
